STEP 1 - Scene: A single whole apple (red-yellow, likely a Gala-type variety) resting on a white square plate. Photographed from directly above (top-down view), so the plate appears nearly undistorted.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The white square plate measures roughly 26 cm across its width, consistent with a dinner plate. Vessel area ≈ 530 cm² (using the plate as the reference; the plate's square shape is approximately 26 x 26 cm, so area is closer to 500-530 cm²).

STEP 3 - Items: One apple. No sauce, oil, or other food visible.

STEP 4 - Area: The apple's visible footprint is about 12-13 cm in diameter in this frame relative to the plate, so roughly 120-130 cm², about 23-25% of the plate.

STEP 5 - Volume: The apple is nearly spherical; its real diameter is about 8 cm, so volume ≈ (4/3)π(4)³ ≈ 268 ml. Using the top-down footprint as a check (~50 cm² x ~7 cm height gives a similar envelope), a gross volume of roughly 250-270 ml is reasonable.

STEP 6 - Grams: Whole fruit has a bulk density near 0.8-0.9 g/ml when treated as a solid object (an apple floats/sinks as a dense whole fruit, about 0.8 g/ml). 260 ml x 0.85 ≈ 220 g. A medium apple typically weighs about 180-200 g, so I'll settle on about 200 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Raw apple ≈ 52 kcal per 100 g. 200 g x 52 = 104 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: One medium apple at roughly 200 g and about 100 kcal is plausible for what is visible. The plate is mostly empty, which is consistent with a small amount of food.

Estimated total: about 200 g, about 104 kcal.
